CAD-COMPLETE-MS0::U-CADC-CRD01.systemImpact: MultiCADSessionEngine is the shared-state floor for every cross-CAD unit in CAD-COMPLETE-MS0 — CrossCADIntentFusionEngine (U-CADC-CRD02) and CrossCADConsistencyValidatorEngine (U-CADC-CRD03) both read its session registry, and CADAccessControlRBACABACEngine (U-FS-12) writes session records into it. Stale-session reaping is an ABA hazard — a sessionId reused after a crashed session can be mistaken for the live one; tag each session record with a monotonic epoch/nonce so a reader detects the reuse rather than acting on a recycled record.

CAD-COMPLETE-MS0::U-CADC-CRD02.systemImpact: CrossCADIntentFusionEngine sits between the heterogeneous intake bridges (sketch/voice/drawing-parse) and the CAD generation pipeline — its fused intent is the input contract for every CAD-COMPLETE-MS0 generation unit. csDepth: Confidence-weighted aggregation needs calibrated source confidences — an uncalibrated voice-parser that always reports 0.9 will dominate a well-calibrated sketch parser; the fusion must normalize or learn per-source reliability priors, not trust raw self-reported confidence.

Embedding-space similarity for intent matching is O(n·d) per query and sensitive to embedding-model version drift — pin the embedding model version in the persisted intent record so a re-embedded prior session is comparable, otherwise cross-session fusion silently degrades.

CAD-COMPLETE-MS0::U-CADC-CRD03.systemImpact: CrossCADConsistencyValidatorEngine is the correctness gate for the multi-CAD generation pipeline — it consumes outputs of U-CADC-CRD01/CRD02 and any CAD bridge, and CAD-UNIVERSAL-CONTROL-MS0's coverage/exit gates (U-CUC15/U-CUC18) depend on it certifying cross-bridge parity. csDepth: Epsilon-tolerance float comparison must be relative-plus-absolute (a fixed absolute epsilon fails on both micron features and meter-scale assemblies) — use scaled tolerance keyed to the part's bounding box, and define it once as a named constant, not inlined per call site.

Geometric hash comparison is order-sensitive — face/edge enumeration order differs across CAD kernels; the hash must canonicalize (sort by a rotation-invariant key) before hashing or identical geometry from two CADs hashes differently and the validator false-fails.

CAD-COMPLETE-MS0::U-CCCO07.systemImpact: U-CCCO07 is a placeholder-titled unit inside CAD-COMPLETE-MS0 — its real downstream consumers cannot be named until the milestone envelope is read. CAD-COMPLETE-MS0::U-FS-04.systemImpact: CADRevisionPromotionWorkflowEngine governs the draft→review→released lifecycle that gates which CAD revision is consumable by downstream CAM and quote pipelines — a released revision is the SSOT a customer order machines against. Concurrent promotion is a classic race: two reviewers both promoting the same revision review→released must be serialized via a per-revision lock or a compare-and-swap on the expected current state, or the second promotion acts on stale state and the released-count diverges.

CAD-COMPLETE-MS0::U-FS-12.systemImpact: CADAccessControlRBACABACEngine is the authorization choke point for every multi-tenant CAD operation — MultiCADSessionEngine (U-CADC-CRD01) writes session records through it and CADTenantNamespaceEngine relies on its tenant-isolation decisions. csDepth: ABAC attribute-policy evaluation can suffer policy-rule ordering bugs and combining-algorithm ambiguity (deny-overrides vs permit-overrides) — the combining algorithm must be explicit and tested with overlapping grant+deny rules, since 'first match wins' silently shadows later deny rules.

RBAC role-permission lookups are hot-path — cache the resolved role→permission matrix but invalidate the cache on role mutation, or a revoked permission stays effective until cache expiry (a security-relevant staleness window).

CAD-COMPLETE-MS0::U-CAD-APP-03.systemImpact: CreoIntegrationTestSuite is the regression net for the Creo CAD bridge — it is what CAD-UNIVERSAL-CONTROL-MS0's coverage exit gate (U-CUC18) counts toward the 95%-by-bridge threshold. COM automation mocking is a hermetic-fakes hazard: a mock that bypasses the real COM marshalling proves nothing about production wiring — at least one fixture must drive the actual Creo API end-to-end as a real-data oracle.

CAD-COMPLETE-MS0::U-CAD-APP-06.systemImpact: CATIAIntegrationTestSuite is the regression net for the CATIA bridge and feeds the CAD-UNIVERSAL-CONTROL-MS0 coverage exit gate (U-CUC18). If its CAA fixtures pass against a fake harness, the coverage gate certifies CATIA support that does not actually work, and CAM/quote pipelines that route CATIA parts fail silently downstream.

CAA automation is process-affine and slow — fixtures should share one CATIA process across the suite (one COM connect/disconnect) rather than spawn per test, but then test isolation must be enforced by explicit document-close between tests or state leaks between cases.

CAD-COMPLETE-MS0::U-CAD-APP-13.systemImpact: CADCrashRecoveryEngine is what keeps a long CAD automation job (e.g. the 20K-file GroundTruthBatchExtractor) survivable across a crash — its watchdog + re-attach + replay is depended on by every long-running CAD bridge operation. If replay double-applies commands, the recovered CAD model diverges from the intended one and silently corrupts whatever pipeline consumes it.
csDepth: Idempotent re-attach requires the command log to carry a monotonic sequence id and the engine to record the last-successfully-applied id atomically before each replay — without it, a crash between 'command applied' and 'log advanced' replays the command and double-applies (an extrude becomes a double-extrude).

Watchdog process supervision must distinguish a wedged-but-alive CAD process from a genuinely dead one — killing a slow-but-progressing process is as harmful as missing a hung one; use a liveness heartbeat plus a progress signal, not PID-existence alone (PID reuse hazard).

CAD-COMPLETE-MS0::U-CAD-APP-16.systemImpact: CADPluginTamperAuditLogEngine is the tamper-evidence layer for CAD plugin command history — security audits and CADAccessControlRBACABACEngine incident review depend on its hash chain being verifiable. If a chain gap is silently skipped instead of failing loud, tampering becomes undetectable and the audit log's entire security value is void.
csDepth: A hash-chained / Merkle log is append-only by construction — concurrent appenders must be serialized through a single writer or a lock, because two writers each hashing the current tip produce a fork; an append-only .jsonl with one canonical writer is the safer data structure than a mutable JSON file.

Chain verification is O(n) over the whole log — for a long-lived CAD plugin this grows unboundedly; checkpoint the chain (periodic signed Merkle roots) so verification can start from the last trusted root rather than genesis, while keeping any gap a hard fail.

CAD-COMPLETE-MS0::U-CAD-APP-19.systemImpact: MastercamHeadlessIntegrationTestSuite fills the cap-11 gap for the #1 CAM app — it is the regression net the CAD-UNIVERSAL-CONTROL-MS0 coverage exit gate (U-CUC18) counts most heavily, since Mastercam is the highest-volume bridge. A suite passing against a fake NET-Hook harness means the most-used CAM bridge is unverified while the coverage gate reports green.
csDepth: Golden-output comparison must be deterministic — Mastercam NET-Hook output can carry timestamps, GUIDs, and machine-specific paths; the golden comparator must normalize those volatile fields or every run false-fails.

The suite must drive the real NET-Hook API in at least one E2E fixture — a 'hermetic fakes don't prove wiring' violation here is high-cost because a missing-from-enum dispatcher action passes a mock 100% while production is 100% broken.

CAD-COMPLETE-MS0::U-ML-11.systemImpact: ContinualLearningBufferEngine (EWC++ + replay buffer) is the catastrophic-forgetting guard for every PRISM learning engine that updates online — CADCAM-AGI's VariabilityIntegrationLayer (U-AGI18) and the CAD learning engines (U-CTE12 targets) depend on it so that adapting to a new customer's parts doesn't erase prior-customer competence. If the Fisher penalty regresses, the model silently forgets old tasks while still reporting good loss on the new one.
csDepth: The Fisher information matrix is O(params²) if stored densely — use the diagonal approximation (standard EWC) and persist only the diagonal, but document that the approximation drops parameter correlations; full Fisher is intractable for any non-trivial model.

Prioritized replay sampling needs a sum-tree (segment tree) for O(log n) proportional sampling and priority update — a naive linear scan over the buffer is O(n) per sample and dominates training time; importance-sampling weights must correct the bias the prioritization introduces.

CAD-COMPLETE-MS0::U-AI-11.systemImpact: SecondOpinionConsensusEngine is the multi-model disagreement-surfacing layer that other AI-routed CAD/CAM units lean on for high-stakes decisions — its design mirrors the 3-of-3 scrutiny gate doctrine. If it silently picks or averages when models diverge (R7 violation), a confidently-wrong single model overrides a correct dissent and the conflict never reaches a human.
csDepth: Quorum voting needs a tie-breaking and abstention policy — with 2 models a disagreement is a 1-1 tie that MUST escalate, not coin-flip; with N models define whether a non-strict majority counts and whether a low-confidence vote abstains rather than votes.

Disagreement detection on free-text outputs is not exact-equality — use semantic divergence (Jaccard over normalized tokens, or embedding cosine distance) with a calibrated threshold; raw string inequality flags trivial paraphrases as disagreement and floods the human queue.

CAD-COMPLETE-MS0::U-INT-07.systemImpact: CADUnitPreferenceEngine resolves the metric/imperial/mixed display and input context for every CAD operation per user/customer — CAD generation, drawing-parse, and CADSTEPAP238Engine (U-INT-10) export all consume its resolved unit system. A lossy or wrong conversion factor here propagates a dimensional error into machined geometry; this is a safety-relevant correctness path, not a cosmetic preference.
csDepth: Unit conversion must use exact rational factors (25.4 mm/in exactly) and apply conversion once at a defined boundary — repeated round-tripping accumulates float error; store dimensions in one canonical internal unit and convert only at the I/O edge.

The per-user/customer/mixed preference fallback chain is a layered-config resolution problem — define a strict precedence order and a deterministic tie-break, and fail loud on an unresolvable 'mixed' spec rather than defaulting silently to one system.

CAD-COMPLETE-MS0::U-INT-08.systemImpact: CADAccessibilityUIAuditEngine audits the CAD frontend UIs against WCAG 2.2 AA — CADRegressionDashboardUI (U-CINF09) and any operator-facing CAD UI depend on it to catch accessibility regressions before release. If it ships toBeDefined-stub checks instead of real contrast/focus-order assertions, the audit reports compliant while the UI is actually unusable for screen-reader/keyboard-only operators.
csDepth: WCAG contrast checks require the WCAG relative-luminance formula with exact sRGB linearization coefficients — an approximate luminance computation flips borderline pass/fail; treat the coefficients as named constants.

Keyboard focus-order traversal is a graph problem — the audit must walk the actual tab-order DAG and detect cycles and unreachable interactive nodes; a flat DOM-order assumption misses CSS/JS-reordered focus and gives false passes.

CAD-COMPLETE-MS0::U-INT-10.systemImpact: CADSTEPAP238Engine exports STEP-NC machining info — its output is the interchange format a downstream CAM/post pipeline (and external machine controllers) consume directly. An AP238 file with malformed part-21 entities is silently unloadable; every CAM consumer that round-trips through STEP-NC inherits the corruption, so write-then-reparse verification is load-bearing.
csDepth: EXPRESS-schema entity emission has ordering and reference-integrity constraints — every entity reference (#id) must resolve and forward references must be permitted by the schema; emit a reference graph and topologically validate it before serialization rather than trusting append order.

Mapping machining features to STEP-NC workingsteps is a many-to-one with unit-system pitfalls — feature dimensions must be in the AP238-mandated units; a metric/imperial mix-up (depends on U-INT-07) emits geometrically valid but dimensionally wrong workingsteps.

CAD-COMPLETE-MS0::U-INT-18.systemImpact: CADCrashRecoveryPlatformEngine is the platform-hardening layer beneath CADCrashRecoveryEngine (U-CAD-APP-13) — it handles orphan COM processes, disk-full checkpoints, and clock-skew. Every long CAD automation job on the memory-pressured PRISM host depends on it; if a disk-full checkpoint corrupts instead of failing loud, recovery replays from a truncated checkpoint and produces a wrong model.
csDepth: Disk-full-safe checkpointing means write-temp-then-rename AND explicitly checking for ENOSPC on both write and fsync — a rename onto a full disk can still fail; the engine must surface ENOSPC loud, never leave a partial checkpoint as the 'latest'.

Clock-skew resilience requires a monotonic clock for ordering recovery events — wall-clock timestamps can go backwards (NTP correction), making a later checkpoint appear older; orphan-COM detection by 'process older than N seconds' must also use monotonic time or a backwards jump reaps a live process.

CAD-GROUND-TRUTH-MS0::U-CGT01.systemImpact: FCStdNativeParserEngine is one of the per-format parsers feeding GroundTruthBatchExtractor (U-CGT07) and the GroundTruthRegistryEngine (U-CGT08) — the ground-truth corpus it produces is the training/validation reference for every CAD ML and regression unit downstream. A parser that silently drops a feature from Document.xml poisons the ground truth, and every model trained on it inherits the gap.
csDepth: FCStd is a ZIP container — entry extraction must guard against zip-slip (a malicious or malformed entry path escaping the extraction root) and against decompression bombs (bounded output size); a 20K-file batch will eventually hit a pathological archive.

FreeCAD Document.xml uses object-reference indirection — features reference each other by name; the parser must build the object graph and resolve references rather than reading a flat element list, or a parametric feature tree is parsed as disconnected nodes.

CAD-GROUND-TRUTH-MS0::U-CGT02.systemImpact: F3DSQLiteParserEngine is the Fusion360 ground-truth parser feeding GroundTruthBatchExtractor (U-CGT07) and the registry (U-CGT08) — the cad-fusion-training-ms0 corpus and Fusion-routed CAD ML units depend on its extraction being faithful. Reading the wrong SQLite table or assuming a schema version that drifted produces silently incomplete ground truth.
csDepth: F3D embeds a real SQLite DB whose schema is version-dependent — query sqlite_master to discover actual table/column names at runtime rather than hardcoding them; the schema-read-first discipline is mandatory here (a recurring META-tool bug class is assuming a schema without reading the file).

Binary-blob columns may hold compressed or proprietary-encoded geometry — the parser must detect and fail loud on an unrecognized blob encoding rather than emitting garbage, and must open the SQLite file read-only to avoid mutating a corpus file.

CAD-GROUND-TRUTH-MS0::U-CGT03.systemImpact: CADToSTEPPipelineEngine is the per-format normalization layer that gives GroundTruthBatchExtractor (U-CGT07) a uniform STEP representation regardless of source CAD — the entire ground-truth corpus's comparability depends on every format-specific pipeline behaving identically through a shared interface. If one format's pipeline emits subtly different STEP, cross-format ground-truth comparison silently breaks.
csDepth: The strategy pattern per format must share a verified common interface contract — divergent error handling between pipelines (one throws, one returns empty) is the silent-degrade hazard; the dispatch table maps extension→pipeline but every pipeline must honor the same fail-loud contract.

STEP geometry export is lossy across kernels — the pipeline should record a fidelity metric (face/edge count delta) per conversion so downstream consumers can filter low-fidelity ground truth rather than treating all conversions as equal.

CAD-GROUND-TRUTH-MS0::U-CGT06.systemImpact: CADScreenshotCapturer produces the reference views that CADVisualDiffEngine and the CAD regression dashboard (U-CINF09) compare against — every visual-diff regression verdict depends on these captures being byte-deterministic. Non-deterministic capture (varying camera, lighting, AA) generates false visual regressions that erode trust in the whole regression suite.
csDepth: Deterministic capture requires pinning camera matrix, light positions, render resolution, anti-aliasing mode, and GPU/software-renderer choice — even driver-version differences in rasterization can flip pixels; pair the capture with perceptual hashing (a small Hamming-distance tolerance) rather than exact pixel equality to absorb sub-perceptual noise.

Perceptual image hashing (pHash/dHash) has a false-negative rate — a real but small geometric change can hash within tolerance; the diff threshold is a precision/recall tradeoff that must be tuned against a labeled set, not guessed.

CAD-GROUND-TRUTH-MS0::U-CGT07.systemImpact: GroundTruthBatchExtractor produces the entire 20K-file ground-truth corpus — it is the single upstream dependency of GroundTruthRegistryEngine (U-CGT08), the CAD ML training units (U-ML-11), and CAD-INFRA-MS0's regression corpus. A crash that restarts from zero instead of resuming wastes hours; a checkpoint bug that skips files silently shrinks the corpus and biases every model trained on it.
csDepth: Bounded-concurrency worker pool: the worker count must be tuned to the memory-pressured PRISM host (commit-memory ceiling), not CPU count — over-subscription triggers the fleet-memory-monitor critical state and OOM; a semaphore-bounded pool with backpressure is the correct structure.

Resumable checkpointing must record per-file completion atomically (an append-only .jsonl of completed file ids) — a checkpoint that records a count rather than the set of done files cannot distinguish 'file 12001-12100 done' from 'a different 100 done', causing skip-or-redo on resume.

CAD-GROUND-TRUTH-MS0::U-CGT08.systemImpact: GroundTruthRegistryEngine is the queryable index over the ground-truth corpus from U-CGT07 — CAD ML training (U-ML-11), regression validation (U-CINF14), and any consistency-validation unit query it by class/feature. If the index is stale or its persisted form is corrupt, every consumer silently trains/validates against a partial corpus.
csDepth: An inverted index keyed by class/feature must be built once and updated incrementally — a linear scan over 20K records per query is O(n) and unusable; the index posting lists should be sorted for fast intersection on multi-term queries.

Persisting the index atomically with schemaVersion is mandatory — a reader hitting a mid-write index file sees truncated JSON; if the index grows large, prefer an append-only or sharded store over rewriting one big JSON, since pretty-printing a multi-hundred-MB structure hits V8's max-string-length cap.

CAD-GROUND-TRUTH-MS0::U-CGT10.systemImpact: The ground-truth determinism regression test is the fail-on-revert oracle that protects the entire CAD-GROUND-TRUTH-MS0 corpus — it guards U-CGT01/02/03/07/08 against silent extraction drift. If this test passes when output drifts, every downstream ML and regression milestone trains against a moving target without knowing it.
csDepth: Determinism verification (same input → byte-identical output) must normalize legitimately non-deterministic fields (timestamps, run ids, absolute paths) before byte-comparison, or it false-fails on noise; the golden file must be regenerable and version-controlled.

A real fail-on-revert oracle must actually fail on the buggy code — write it so that reverting the determinism fix flips the test red; a test that passes against both correct and buggy output is a worthless toBeDefined-class stub.

CAD-INFRA-MS0::U-CINF01.systemImpact: CADFileIndexerEngine is the master 20,006-file catalog that CADFileClassifierEngine (U-CINF02), the CAD universal-control coverage telemetry (U-CUC16), and the new-customer-directory watcher (U-CUC05) all read. If the incremental mtime-keyed update misses a changed file, the entire CAD coverage picture and every downstream classifier silently operates on a stale catalog.
csDepth: mtime-keyed incremental indexing has a known false-negative: a file modified within the same second as the last index pass, or restored with a preserved mtime, is missed — pair mtime with size and optionally a content hash for changed-file detection; bounded-depth recursion prevents runaway on symlink loops.

Persisting a 20K-entry catalog atomically means temp+rename, and at this scale prefer not pretty-printing the JSON (compact stringify) — the system-viz fs-coverage work documents the V8 max-string-length crash from indented stringify of large merged graphs.

CAD-INFRA-MS0::U-CINF02.systemImpact: CADFileClassifierEngine labels every cataloged file part/assembly/drawing/CAM — CAD-INFRA-MS0's regression infra (U-CINF14 smoke corpus) and coverage telemetry (U-CUC16) partition work by these classes. A misclassification routes a file to the wrong test/extraction lane, so a drawing tested as a part silently produces a false regression or a skipped check.
csDepth: Extension-only classification is unreliable (.dwg can be a drawing or, mislabeled, an assembly export) — combine the file magic-number/content signature with the extension; assert every class branch with a real example file so the decision tree's leaves are all exercised.

An 'unknown/other' bucket must be surfaced loudly, not silently swallowed — an unclassified file is a coverage gap; a rule classifier should emit a confidence and route low-confidence cases to a human-review queue.

CAD-INFRA-MS0::U-CINF03.systemImpact: CADTestStateSchema defines the per-file atomic state record that CADTestCheckpointEngine (U-CINF05), CADFailureTriageEngine (U-CINF06), and CADRegressionResultsAnalyzerEngine (U-CINF10) all read and write — it is the shared data contract for the whole CAD regression pipeline. A schema change without a migration path breaks every consumer at once.
csDepth: Per-file atomic state means each file's state record is its own temp+rename write — this avoids the multi-writer race entirely (no shared mutable JSON), and a reader hitting a mid-write file must never see truncated JSON; the rename is the atomicity guarantee.

Every state JSON requires schemaVersion and an N-1 backward-compatible migration — a Zod schema validates on read, but the analyzer must read schemaVersion FIRST and dispatch to the right field mapping; assuming current field names against an older record is the recurring schema-read-blindness bug class.

CAD-INFRA-MS0::U-CINF05.systemImpact: CADTestCheckpointEngine makes the CAD regression run resumable every 100 files — the 20K-file regression sweep (and U-CINF14's smoke validation) depends on it so a crash at file 12K resumes rather than restarts. A checkpoint bug that skips or re-runs files corrupts CADRegressionResultsAnalyzerEngine's (U-CINF10) aggregate pass-rate.
csDepth: The checkpoint must record the SET of completed file ids (append-only), not a count — restart logic that resumes 'after file N' assumes processing order is stable; if order varies (parallel workers), only an explicit done-set lets resume skip exactly the done files.

Atomic checkpoint write (temp+rename) every 100 files is a throughput/durability tradeoff — too-frequent checkpointing serializes the workers on fsync; the 100-file interval bounds re-work to at most 100 files on a crash, which is the right granularity.

CAD-INFRA-MS0::U-CINF06.systemImpact: CADFailureTriageEngine classifies every CAD regression failure into a named category — CADRegressionResultsAnalyzerEngine (U-CINF10), the dashboard (U-CINF09), and the safety hooks (U-CINF13) all consume its taxonomy to decide aggregate health and whether to abort. An uncategorized failure falling into a silent 'unknown' bucket hides a whole class of breakage from the abort gate.
csDepth: Exception-type-to-category mapping must have a total function semantics — every failure lands in a named category, and a genuinely new exception type must surface as a LOUD 'needs-a-rule' finding, not default into an 'unknown' sink that the analyzer then under-weights.

Rule-based triage ordering matters: a broad rule placed before a specific one shadows it (the same first-match-wins shadowing hazard as ABAC policy ordering); order rules specific-to-general and test the overlap cases.

CAD-INFRA-MS0::U-CINF07.systemImpact: CADArtifactStorageEngine content-addresses the diffs/images/logs produced by the CAD regression run — CADRegressionDashboardUI (U-CINF09) and CADRegressionReportGeneratorEngine (U-CINF11) link to its blobs. If two identical artifacts don't dedupe, storage bloats; if a blob write is non-atomic, the dashboard links to a truncated image.
csDepth: Content-addressable storage keyed by SHA-256 gives free deduplication but a hash collision (astronomically unlikely with SHA-256, but a malformed-input bug can compute the wrong hash) writes one blob over another — verify hash on read for safety-relevant artifacts.

Atomic blob write (temp+rename into the hash-named final path) makes the store idempotent: re-storing an identical artifact is a no-op; this also makes concurrent writers safe since both produce the same final name and the rename is atomic.

CAD-INFRA-MS0::U-CINF09.systemImpact: CADRegressionDashboardUI is the operator-facing surface for the whole CAD regression infra — it renders CADRegressionResultsAnalyzerEngine's (U-CINF10) aggregate metrics and CADArtifactStorageEngine's (U-CINF07) artifacts. If it renders hardcoded placeholder data, operators trust a green dashboard while real regressions go unnoticed.
csDepth: The dashboard must render purely from the regression results JSON — no derived metrics computed in the UI layer, or the dashboard and the analyzer disagree (two surfaces, one metric, two answers); the analyzer is the single source of truth.

React state management for a large result set needs virtualization/pagination — rendering 20K result rows in one DOM tree is a performance cliff; the API endpoint should serve paginated/aggregated slices, not the raw set.

CAD-INFRA-MS0::U-CINF10.systemImpact: CADRegressionResultsAnalyzerEngine is the metric authority for CAD regression — CADRegressionDashboardUI (U-CINF09), CADRegressionReportGeneratorEngine (U-CINF11), CADRegressionSafetyHooks (U-CINF13's abort threshold), and the CAD-UNIVERSAL coverage gate (U-CUC16/U-CUC18) all consume its aggregate pass-rate/percentiles. A wrong aggregation silently mis-certifies milestone exit gates.
csDepth: Aggregation must be a streaming reduce over result records (not load-all-into-memory) at 20K scale — and percentile computation needs the full distribution; use a t-digest or sorted-sample structure for streaming percentiles rather than an exact sort of all values.

Read the result-state schemaVersion before mapping field names — the recurring META-tool bug (high-roi-skill-rank reading totals.* against a v2 top-level schema) is exactly this class: assume nothing about field shape, schema-probe first.

CAD-INFRA-MS0::U-CINF11.systemImpact: CADRegressionReportGeneratorEngine produces the PDF/HTML reports operators and stakeholders read for CAD regression runs — it consumes CADRegressionResultsAnalyzerEngine's (U-CINF10) aggregate JSON. A malformed report or one built from stale/placeholder metrics misinforms the milestone close-out decision.
csDepth: PDF/HTML generation from structured data must round-trip-verify the output is well-formed (parse the generated HTML, validate the PDF opens) — a write-only report generator can emit broken markup that renders blank.

The report must reflect the analyzer's metrics verbatim — recomputing any metric in the report layer creates a divergence; consume the analyzer JSON as the single source and template over it, write the report file atomically.

CAD-INFRA-MS0::U-CINF13.systemImpact: CADRegressionSafetyHooks abort a CAD regression run on cascading failure — they protect the host (a 20K-file run that's failing every file wastes hours and memory) and prevent a corrupt run from feeding CADRegressionResultsAnalyzerEngine (U-CINF10) a meaningless aggregate. If the abort gate doesn't fire, a cascade runs to completion and the dashboard reports a falsely-low pass-rate as if it were real signal.
csDepth: The circuit-breaker needs a failure-rate window, not a raw count — abort on 'N failures in the last M files', because an absolute count would never abort a long run with a steady low failure rate while a true cascade should trip fast; tune the window against real failure-burst data.

The abort must be loud and idempotent — once tripped it stays tripped for the run; a flapping breaker (trip, recover, trip) on a borderline failure rate produces a half-finished run that's worse than either a clean abort or a clean completion.

CAD-INFRA-MS0::U-CINF14.systemImpact: The 100-file smoke corpus is the fast CI gate for the CAD regression infra — it runs before the full 20K sweep and is the practical fail-on-revert oracle for U-CINF01 through U-CINF13. If the smoke corpus is unrepresentative or its assertions are stubs, a CAD extraction regression ships green and only surfaces in production.
csDepth: Smoke-corpus subset selection must cover every file class (part/assembly/drawing/CAM) and every parser path — a 100-file sample that accidentally omits a class gives no coverage for that path; stratified sampling, not random, is correct here.

Deterministic 100-file validation means the same 100 files in the same order produce byte-identical aggregate output — the test fails loud on any extraction regression, and reverting any U-CINF fix must flip it red, or it is not a real oracle.

CAD-INFRA-MS0::U-CINF15.systemImpact: The CAD regression infra documentation + runbook is the operator's recovery and operating reference for U-CINF01 through U-CINF14 — without it, a stalled or aborted regression run has no documented restart path and the infra becomes operator-opaque. It is also the doc surface the doc-reflection rule requires updating when any U-CINF unit changes.
csDepth: Documentation-as-code means the runbook lives in-repo and is kept current by the doc-reflection rule — a runbook that drifts from the actual recovery procedure is worse than none, because operators trust a stale procedure.
The runbook should be a concise pointer index (claude-md-as-pointer-index discipline) into the wiki detail pages, not a monolith — past ~200 lines, dense operational docs stop being read.

CAD-TRAINING-EXTRACT-MS0::U-CTE01.systemImpact: Extracting the Mastercam Basics tutorial feeds structured KnowledgeTip records into the knowledge-conversion lanes that the CAM learning engines and tribal corpus consume — U-CTE11 (action-sequence index) and U-CTE12 (wire into learning engines) depend on this extraction's output. Malformed extraction poisons the tip corpus that recommendation engines query.
csDepth: Document-to-structured-knowledge extraction must dedupe against the already-extracted Mastercam(45) set before adding — the duplicationGuardEngine / extraction-log discipline; re-extracting an existing tutorial double-counts tips and biases retrieval.

Tutorial step parsing is sequence extraction — preserve step ordering and the action→parameter binding; a parser that flattens steps into a bag-of-tips loses the procedural structure the learning engines need.

CAD-TRAINING-EXTRACT-MS0::U-CTE02.systemImpact: Extracting the Mastercam Solids tutorial adds solid-modeling KnowledgeTip records to the corpus feeding U-CTE11's action-sequence index and U-CTE12's learning-engine ingestion — it shares the Mastercam extraction lane with U-CTE01 and U-CTE03, so consistent schema across all three is what makes the consolidated index coherent.
csDepth: Dedupe against already-extracted Mastercam(45) AND against U-CTE01's output — overlapping basics/solids content double-counts; the extraction registry is the cross-unit dedup authority.

Solid-modeling step parsing must capture feature-tree operations (extrude/revolve/boolean) with their parameters — these are parametric actions; extracting prose without the parameter bindings yields tips the learning engine can't act on.

CAD-TRAINING-EXTRACT-MS0::U-CTE03.systemImpact: Extracting Mastercam Wire EDM tutorials feeds the EDM knowledge lane — the WEDM AGI engines (62 of them) and the wire-EDM studios consume EDM-specific tips. If wire/flush/taper parameters are lost in extraction, the EDM learning corpus is missing exactly the parameters that distinguish wire-EDM from milling knowledge.
csDepth: EDM action-sequence parsing must preserve EDM-specific parameter dimensions (wire diameter, flush pressure, taper angle) and their units — these are not milling parameters; a generic CAM extractor that drops them silently strips the EDM signal.
Dedupe against the existing 46 WEDM tribal tips — the EDM corpus is already substantial; re-extracting overlapping content biases the WEDM retrieval index.

CAD-TRAINING-EXTRACT-MS0::U-CTE04.systemImpact: Extracting InventorCAM 2.5D Milling + 3D HSM strategy knowledge feeds the CAM strategy lane — the strategy-selection and toolpath engines consume these strategy records, and U-CTE11's action-sequence index incorporates them. Mis-extracted HSM strategy knowledge degrades automated strategy recommendation.
csDepth: 2.5D vs 3D-HSM strategies have distinct parameter spaces (stepover/stepdown vs constant-engagement/scallop) — the extractor must keep them in separate strategy categories or the learning engine conflates two regimes.

Extraction stays advisory until human-verified — a strategy tip that drives a real toolpath is safety-relevant; mark mustHumanVerify on the ledger, never auto-wire raw extracted strategy into a generator.

CAD-TRAINING-EXTRACT-MS0::U-CTE05.systemImpact: Extracting the three InventorCAM 5-axis training volumes feeds the 5-axis CAM knowledge lane consumed by the 5-axis engines and strategy selection — three volumes consolidating into one action-sequence set means cross-volume dedup quality directly determines whether the 5-axis tip corpus is coherent or has triplicated entries.
csDepth: Multi-document corpus consolidation across three volumes is a merge-with-dedup problem — overlapping topics must be detected by semantic similarity, not exact title match; near-duplicate tips across volumes inflate retrieval weight.

5-axis training extraction must preserve tool-axis-orientation and kinematic-mode context — a 5-axis strategy tip without its kinematics is ambiguous; the extractor must keep the multi-axis context that distinguishes 5-axis from 3-axis advice.

CAD-TRAINING-EXTRACT-MS0::U-CTE06.systemImpact: Extracting InventorCAM Advanced + iLogic knowledge feeds the CAM strategy lane plus the parametric-rule knowledge that drives Inventor automation (relevant to InventorILogicBridgeEngine, U-AGI07). iLogic is parametric scripting — extracting the rule logic, not just prose, is what makes this extraction actionable for the bridge engines.
csDepth: iLogic / parametric-rule extraction must capture the rule's conditional logic and parameter dependencies as structured data — prose extraction loses the executable semantics; the rule is closer to code than to a tip.
Advanced-strategy parsing should record the precondition context (when the advanced strategy applies) so the learning engine can match it to a situation, not just store it as a flat fact.

CAD-TRAINING-EXTRACT-MS0::U-CTE07.systemImpact: Extracting SolidWorks training feeds the CAD modeling-knowledge lane consumed by U-CTE11's action-sequence index and the CAD learning engines (U-CTE12) — registering through the extraction-training registry is what prevents the same SolidWorks corpus being ingested twice across training-extract units.
csDepth: Modeling-feature step parsing must capture the SolidWorks feature-tree operation order and parent-child references — a flattened feature list loses the dependency structure a modeling-recommendation engine needs.

Registering through the extraction-training registry is the idempotency guarantee — re-running the extraction must be a no-op for already-registered content; without the registry, a re-run double-ingests.

CAD-TRAINING-EXTRACT-MS0::U-CTE08.systemImpact: Extracting Fusion 360 training (CAM + tools) feeds the CAM and tool-knowledge lanes; it shares the Fusion corpus with cad-fusion-training-ms0, so cross-referencing that corpus is what prevents re-extracting already-ingested Fusion content into the action-sequence index (U-CTE11).
csDepth: Cross-reference the cad-fusion-training-ms0 corpus before extraction — overlapping Fusion content already extracted there must be deduped, or the Fusion tip corpus double-counts.

CAM + tool knowledge are two distinct lanes (toolpath strategy vs tool-library data) — keep them in separate KnowledgeTip categories so tool-selection retrieval doesn't get strategy tips and vice versa.

CAD-TRAINING-EXTRACT-MS0::U-CTE09.systemImpact: Extracting FreeCAD Path Workbench knowledge from online sources feeds the CAM knowledge lane — it is the knowledge backing for FreeCADPathBridgeEngine (U-AGI05), so the Path Workbench API surface this extraction captures directly determines what the bridge can drive.
csDepth: Online-source extraction must attribute and pin source URLs + retrieval dates — web content drifts; an un-attributed tip can't be re-verified, and a stale extraction silently encodes an outdated API.

Capturing the Path Workbench API surface is an inventory problem — the extraction should produce a structured operation/parameter list, not prose, so the bridge engine can map PRISM CAM ops onto real Path calls.

CAD-TRAINING-EXTRACT-MS0::U-CTE10.systemImpact: Consolidating scattered hyperMILL extractions into coherent action sequences is a cleanup unit — it produces the canonical hyperMILL action-sequence set that U-CTE11's index and U-CTE12's learning-engine ingestion consume. Without consolidation, the hyperMILL knowledge is fragmented across documents and retrieval is incoherent.
csDepth: Action-sequence consolidation across documents is a merge + dedup over the already-extracted hyperMILL(25) set — overlapping sequences must be unified, not concatenated; semantic dedup, not exact match.

Consolidation must preserve sequence boundaries — merging two partial sequences into one only when they're genuinely the same procedure; an over-eager merge fuses distinct procedures into a nonsensical combined sequence.

CAD-TRAINING-EXTRACT-MS0::U-CTE11.systemImpact: The CAD Action Sequence Index is the queryable retrieval layer over every U-CTE01..U-CTE10 extraction — U-CTE12 (wire into learning engines) and any build-resolution / strategy-recommendation consumer queries it. If the index is stale or non-atomic, every downstream learning engine retrieves against a partial action-sequence corpus.
csDepth: An action-sequence index combining an inverted index (by class/feature) and an embedding-based retrieval index has two consistency surfaces — both must be rebuilt together when the corpus changes, or keyword and semantic retrieval disagree.

Embedding-based retrieval must pin the embedding model version in the index (the 14,738 int8 768-d nomic-embed vectors precedent) — a re-embedded query against an index built with a different model silently returns wrong neighbors; persist atomically with schemaVersion.

CAD-TRAINING-EXTRACT-MS0::U-CTE12.systemImpact: Wiring action sequences into the CAD learning engines is the consumption step that makes the entire CAD-TRAINING-EXTRACT-MS0 milestone payoff real — CADTrialErrorLearningEngine and CamFeatureLearningEngine ingest the U-CTE11 index, and their recommend() output then drives CAD/CAM automation. If the ingest API is mis-wired, the milestone shipped extraction with no consumer (the writer-without-reader anti-pattern).
csDepth: Batch ingestion into a learning engine must be idempotent — re-ingesting the same sequences must not double-weight patterns; the engine's ingest API needs a dedup key (sequence id) so a re-run is safe.

The acceptance test must verify recommend() returns the ingested patterns end-to-end through the real ingest API — a test against a fake ingest path proves nothing about production wiring (the hermetic-fakes hazard); this is the round-trip oracle.

CAD-UNIVERSAL-CONTROL-MS0::U-CUC04.systemImpact: The unknown-extension detector is the coverage-gap surface for CAD-UNIVERSAL-CONTROL-MS0 — it feeds the coverage telemetry (U-CUC16) and the exit gate (U-CUC18) by naming every unrecognized file. A detector that stays silent on an unknown extension hides exactly the gap the 95%-coverage milestone gate exists to measure.
csDepth: The detector is a set-difference of seen-extensions minus known/supported-extensions — the known set is an allowlist that must be the single source of truth shared with the format-conversion matrix, or the detector and the converters disagree on what's 'known'.

Surfacing must be loud but not noisy — append one advisory per newly-seen unknown extension, dedup against already-surfaced ones (a stamp/seen-set), so a recurring unknown extension doesn't spam every run.

CAD-UNIVERSAL-CONTROL-MS0::U-CUC05.systemImpact: The new-customer-directory watcher (Stop hook, debounced hourly) keeps CADFileIndexerEngine's catalog and the CAD coverage telemetry current as customers are added — it is the freshness mechanism behind U-CUC16's coverage numbers. If the debounce fails, either it never sweeps (stale coverage) or it sweeps every Stop (host load spike across the 13-chat fleet).
csDepth: Stop-hook debounce via a stamp file is the standard pattern — many simultaneous Stops collapse to one sweep; the stamp's mtime gates the next run, and the throttle interval must be read at call-time so an env override takes effect.

Directory-change detection by mtime/stamp has the same same-second false-negative as mtime indexing — a customer directory created and a file added within the throttle window may be partially seen; the watcher should re-sweep from the last stamp boundary, not from 'now'.

CAD-UNIVERSAL-CONTROL-MS0::U-CUC06.systemImpact: The volume-delta alert posts to AGENT_CHAT when extension-volume shifts >5% vs baseline — it is the operator early-warning that the CAD corpus changed materially, feeding into coverage-gate re-evaluation (U-CUC16). It mirrors the fleet-memory-monitor's single-advisory-line discipline; over-alerting trains operators to ignore it.
csDepth: Delta detection vs a stored baseline needs the baseline to be updatable — after an alert fires and the operator acknowledges, the baseline should advance, or every subsequent run re-fires the same >5% alert (alert fatigue).

Appending to AGENT_CHAT must be a single advisory line with a cooldown — concurrent appenders need atomic append (an append-only .jsonl), and the >5% threshold must be hysteretic (don't flap at exactly 5%).

CAD-UNIVERSAL-CONTROL-MS0::U-CUC07.systemImpact: DxfWriterEngine (pure-JS DXF generator) is a P0 coverage gap — it gives CAD-UNIVERSAL-CONTROL-MS0 a no-dependency DXF export path counted toward the U-CUC18 95%-by-bridge exit gate, and the write-path integration tests (U-CUC17) verify it. Every consumer that needs DXF output (drawings, CAM interchange) depends on it emitting loadable files.
csDepth: DXF is a group-code text format — each entity is (group-code, value) pairs in the ENTITIES section; the writer must emit the exact group codes for each entity type per the AutoCAD R12/2000 spec, and a wrong code produces a file that reads as a different entity.
Round-trip verification (write then re-parse) is mandatory — a write-only DXF test that checks 'no exception thrown' proves nothing; the test must re-import and assert entity counts/geometry match.

CAD-UNIVERSAL-CONTROL-MS0::U-CUC08.systemImpact: Mastercam native save (.mcx-8/.mcx/.mcx-6) is a P0 coverage gap — it gives CAD-UNIVERSAL-CONTROL-MS0 the ability to write Mastercam-native files for the #1 CAM app, counted toward the U-CUC18 exit gate. Without it, parts routed through the Mastercam bridge can be read but not saved back natively.
csDepth: .mcx is a proprietary binary format — native save almost certainly requires the NET-Hook automation API per Mastercam version; the engine must dispatch on version (.mcx-6/.mcx/.mcx-8) and fail loud if the required Mastercam version isn't installed.

Verify each version writes a loadable file (re-open it) — a binary-format writer that emits a structurally-wrong file is silently broken; version-specific format dispatch must be tested per version, not assumed uniform.

CAD-UNIVERSAL-CONTROL-MS0::U-CUC09.systemImpact: The DWG bridge (ODA File Converter or LibreDWG) is a P1 coverage gap — it gives CAD-UNIVERSAL-CONTROL-MS0 DWG read/write via an external converter, counted toward the U-CUC18 exit gate. As a subprocess bridge it is also a reliability surface: a converter-missing or nonzero-exit case must fail loud, not produce a silent empty file.
csDepth: External-converter subprocess bridging must handle three failure modes explicitly: converter-binary-missing (ENOENT on spawn), nonzero exit code, and zero-exit-but-empty-output — each must fail loud; a converter that 'succeeds' but produces a 0-byte DWG is the silent-corruption hazard.
Subprocess invocation needs a timeout and bounded output capture — a hung ODA converter would otherwise wedge the calling pipeline; capture stderr for diagnostics since a SIGKILL leaves no message.

CAD-UNIVERSAL-CONTROL-MS0::U-CUC10.systemImpact: Inventor .idw drawing export is a P2 coverage gap — it gives CAD-UNIVERSAL-CONTROL-MS0 the ability to emit Inventor drawing documents via COM automation, counted toward the U-CUC18 exit gate and verified by U-CUC17's write-path tests.
csDepth: Inventor .idw export drives the COM automation API — it requires Inventor installed and a live COM connection; the engine must fail loud on Inventor-not-running, not return a fake success.

Verification must open the exported .idw and assert the expected views are present — a COM export call that returns without error can still produce a drawing with missing or empty view placeholders; check the actual document contents.

CAD-UNIVERSAL-CONTROL-MS0::U-CUC11.systemImpact: STL via CadQuery is a P2 coverage gap — a thin wrapper giving CAD-UNIVERSAL-CONTROL-MS0 STL export through the Python CAD kernel, counted toward the U-CUC18 exit gate. STL output feeds mesh-based downstream consumers (StltoVoxelGridEngine, 3D-print/visualization paths).
csDepth: Even a 'trivial wrapper' must pass mesh-resolution parameters through — a wrapper that calls export with default tessellation silently produces a coarse mesh; the test must verify the resolution param actually changes triangle count.
The Python CAD-kernel bridge crosses a process boundary — handle Python-missing and CadQuery-import-error fail-loud; a wrapper that swallows the subprocess error returns an empty STL silently.

CAD-UNIVERSAL-CONTROL-MS0::U-CUC12.systemImpact: Parasolid .x_b/.x_t support is a P3 coverage gap — it gives CAD-UNIVERSAL-CONTROL-MS0 Parasolid interchange via a STEP round-trip, counted toward the U-CUC18 exit gate. Because it round-trips through STEP, it inherits STEP's lossy-conversion risk for any consumer of Parasolid geometry.
csDepth: STEP round-trip conversion of B-rep geometry risks losing faces/edges/topology — the test must assert B-rep fidelity (face count, edge count, watertightness) survives the round-trip, not just that a file was produced.
Parasolid .x_b (binary) vs .x_t (text) are two encodings of the same kernel format — the engine must handle both; a writer that only does .x_t silently can't satisfy a .x_b request.

CAD-UNIVERSAL-CONTROL-MS0::U-CUC13.systemImpact: The IGES .igs translator is a P3 coverage gap — it gives CAD-UNIVERSAL-CONTROL-MS0 IGES interchange, counted toward the U-CUC18 exit gate and verified by U-CUC17's write-path tests. IGES is a legacy interchange format still common in customer file archives.
csDepth: IGES is a fixed-72-column record format with five sections (Start/Global/Directory/Parameter/Terminate) — the parser must respect exact column positions and the Directory-Entry→Parameter-Data linkage; a column-offset error shifts every field and silently mis-parses.

IGES uses parameter and record delimiters declared in the Global section — the parser must read those delimiters first, not assume the defaults (comma/semicolon); a file with non-default delimiters breaks a hardcoded parser.

CAD-UNIVERSAL-CONTROL-MS0::U-CUC14.systemImpact: Natural-language CAD routing tests verify that SlashCommandRecommender + AgentRegistry route real prompts to the correct CAD bridge — they are the regression net for the NL-routing layer that the whole CAD-UNIVERSAL-CONTROL-MS0 user-facing entry depends on. A routing regression silently sends a CAD request to the wrong bridge.
csDepth: NL intent classification is a precision/recall tradeoff — the tests must include near-miss prompts (phrases close to two bridges) and assert the right one wins, not just easy unambiguous prompts; an ambiguous prompt should surface the ambiguity, not silently pick.

Keyword + similarity routing has a polysemy hazard (e.g. a token matching multiple domains) — tests must pin the disambiguation rule with concrete example phrases, the way the /lathe polysemy guard does.

CAD-UNIVERSAL-CONTROL-MS0::U-CUC15.systemImpact: The coverage regression smoke test drives all 6 CAD bridges through prism_ai and asserts each responds — it is the integration oracle for the U-CUC18 exit gate. If it passes against mocks, a bridge missing from the dispatcher enum looks healthy while production is 100% broken for that bridge.
csDepth: The smoke test must drive the REAL prism_ai dispatcher, not a MockMCPServer — the documented RGS-TOOL bug is that a mock bypasses the z.enum(ACTIONS) gate, so a missing-from-enum action 9/9-passes while production is fully broken; this test must round-trip through the real enum gate.
Coverage-gap detection across N bridges is a set-coverage assertion — the test must enumerate all 6 expected bridges and fail loud if any is absent, not just check that 'some' bridge responded.

CAD-UNIVERSAL-CONTROL-MS0::U-CUC16.systemImpact: CAD-coverage volume telemetry feeds the SVI-gated milestone gate — it computes by-extension and by-volume coverage from CADFileIndexerEngine's catalog and gates the U-CUC18 milestone exit. If the telemetry mis-computes, the gate either blocks a complete milestone or passes an incomplete one.
csDepth: Coverage must be computed two ways (by-extension count AND by-file-volume) because they answer different questions — a format with few files but huge volume can pass by-count and fail by-volume; the gate ANDs both, so both computations must be correct.

The telemetry must derive from a single source (the file index) — the viz-coverage-ms0 precedent is that a hand-edited domain-count array drifted from BUILD_STATE; coverage figures must be computed from the canonical catalog, not maintained separately.

CAD-UNIVERSAL-CONTROL-MS0::U-CUC17.systemImpact: Write-path integration tests per bridge verify export correctness for DxfWriterEngine (U-CUC07), Mastercam save (U-CUC08), DWG (U-CUC09), .idw (U-CUC10), STL (U-CUC11), Parasolid (U-CUC12), IGES (U-CUC13) — they are the regression net the U-CUC18 exit gate counts. A write test that only checks 'no exception' lets a corrupt exporter pass.
csDepth: Write-path tests must export then re-import to verify the file is genuinely valid — the round-trip is the real assertion; 'no exception thrown' on write proves nothing about whether the file is loadable.

Per-bridge fixture parameterization should share one parameterized harness across all 7 export bridges so coverage is uniform — divergent ad-hoc tests per bridge leave inconsistent assertion strength and a weak bridge slips through.

CAD-UNIVERSAL-CONTROL-MS0::U-CUC18.systemImpact: The CAD-UNIVERSAL-CONTROL-MS0 milestone exit gate is the final certification for the whole milestone — it ANDs coverage>=95% by-ext AND by-volume (U-CUC16) AND all ingestion mechanisms live (U-CUC05) AND AI routing canaries pass (U-CUC14/U-CUC15). A weak gate ships an incomplete milestone as done, creating exactly the silent-close-out-drift the close-out audit exists to catch.
csDepth: A multi-criterion gate must AND every criterion and report WHICH criterion failed — a gate that returns a single boolean with no breakdown gives the operator no actionable signal; each of the four criteria must be a real measured check, not a hardcoded pass.
Canary tests must be genuine fail-on-revert oracles — a canary that passes regardless of whether the AI routing works is a toBeDefined stub; reverting any routing fix must flip a canary red.

CADCAM-AGI-MS0::U-AGI01.systemImpact: LOCBasedAdaptiveParameterEngine is a core CADCAM-AGI engine — the AGI master controller (U-AGI03) and the cycle-time/speed-feed optimizers consume its LOC-adapted parameters. Because it scales feeds by engagement, a regression here directly changes cutting parameters: an over-aggressive feed is a tool-breakage / safety hazard, so it must import Kienzle/material constants from physics/constants.ts.
csDepth: Engagement-angle to feed scaling must clamp to a safe envelope — an adaptive control loop without saturation limits can command a feed outside the machine/tool capability; the clamp bounds are safety constants, not tunables.

LOC-based adaptation is a control loop — it must be stable (no oscillation): a poorly-damped feed response chatters; pair the gain with a rate limiter and verify against a real cutting sequence that would oscillate without damping.

CADCAM-AGI-MS0::U-AGI03.systemImpact: CADCAMAGIOrchestrationEngine is the master controller for the entire CADCAM-AGI-MS0 milestone — it sequences every sub-engine (U-AGI01, U-AGI04..U-AGI19) and is wired by cadCamAgiDispatcher (U-AGI20). If a sub-engine isn't wired in the same commit it becomes an orphan; if a stage failure is swallowed, the whole AGI pipeline produces a wrong program from a silently-skipped stage.
csDepth: The sub-engine dependency graph must be a DAG with explicit stage ordering — a cycle means non-termination; topologically sort stages and fail loud on a cycle, since the orchestrator can't sequence a cyclic dependency.

A stage failure must propagate and abort the pipeline (fail-loud) — an orchestrator that catches a sub-engine error and continues produces a program missing that stage's contribution, which is worse than a clean abort; partial output must never be presented as complete.

CADCAM-AGI-MS0::U-AGI04.systemImpact: CadQueryBridgeEngine is the Python CAD-kernel bridge that gives CADCAM-AGI parametric/B-rep geometry operations — CadQueryActionExecutorEngine (U-DASAL02) and any AGI unit needing real geometry depend on it. As a process-boundary bridge it is a reliability surface: a swallowed Python error silently returns no geometry.
csDepth: JSON IPC across the process boundary must define a strict request/response schema and handle partial reads — a CAD-kernel subprocess can emit large geometry payloads; the bridge must frame messages (length-prefixed or delimiter) so a chunked read doesn't truncate.

Python-missing, OCCT-import-error, and subprocess-crash are three distinct failure modes — each must fail loud with a distinguishable error; a bridge that returns an empty result for all three hides the root cause.

CADCAM-AGI-MS0::U-AGI05.systemImpact: FreeCADPathBridgeEngine integrates FreeCAD CAM into CADCAM-AGI — the AGI orchestrator (U-AGI03) routes CAM operations through it, and it is the runtime consumer of the FreeCAD Path knowledge extracted in U-CTE09. A mistranslated CAM op produces a wrong toolpath that the safety gate (U-AGI24) must then catch downstream.
csDepth: CAM operation translation from PRISM ops to Path Workbench calls is a mapping that must be total — an unmapped PRISM op must fail loud, not silently emit no toolpath; every op needs an explicit Path-call equivalent or a documented rejection.

Generated toolpaths must be verified against a real FreeCAD Path job — a translation that produces syntactically valid Path calls but geometrically wrong toolpaths is the silent-correctness hazard; verify the toolpath, not just that the calls executed.

CADCAM-AGI-MS0::U-AGI06.systemImpact: MastercamAutomationBridgeEngine is the .NET automation bridge for the #1 CAM app within CADCAM-AGI — the AGI orchestrator (U-AGI03) drives Mastercam through it. As COM/.NET automation it must handle Mastercam-not-running and COM-error fail-loud, or the AGI pipeline silently produces nothing while reporting success.
csDepth: COM automation is process-affine and stateful — the bridge must manage the Mastercam process lifecycle (connect, keep-alive, disconnect) and detect a wedged COM connection; a stale COM reference throws RPC_E_DISCONNECTED unpredictably.

Each automation call must be verified for its real effect (the geometry/toolpath actually changed), not just a non-throwing return — a COM call can return success while the operation no-op'd; verify the effect.

CADCAM-AGI-MS0::U-AGI07.systemImpact: InventorILogicBridgeEngine is the parametric CAD driver for CADCAM-AGI — the AGI orchestrator (U-AGI03) and the parametric-part library use it to drive Inventor models by rule. The iLogic knowledge extracted in U-CTE06 is its knowledge backing. A rule that doesn't actually regenerate the model produces a stale part silently.
csDepth: iLogic rule-driven regeneration is order-dependent — parameter changes must trigger a full feature-tree regeneration and the bridge must verify the model actually rebuilt (not just that the parameter was set); an un-regenerated model is silently stale.

COM automation for parametric CAD must distinguish a regeneration FAILURE (constraint conflict, over-defined sketch) from success — Inventor can leave the model in an error state; the bridge must report that loud, not treat 'returned' as 'succeeded'.

CADCAM-AGI-MS0::U-AGI09.systemImpact: StockAutoSelectionChainEngine picks inventory-aware stock for CADCAM-AGI — the AGI orchestrator (U-AGI03) consumes its choice, and cycle-time/cost optimizers downstream depend on the stock dimension. A wrong stock selection cascades into wrong machining-allowance and cost estimates.
csDepth: A chain-of-responsibility selection must have a deterministic fall-through — when no stock matches, the chain must terminate in an explicit 'no stock available' result, not silently return the last-tried candidate; the order of handlers determines the selection bias.

Inventory-aware constraint satisfaction is a small optimization (minimize waste subject to fitting the part) — but it must read LIVE inventory; a selection against a stale inventory snapshot picks stock that's already consumed, a race with the ERP system.

CADCAM-AGI-MS0::U-AGI11.systemImpact: ToolAutoSelectionChainEngine selects tooling for CADCAM-AGI by matching feature+material to the tool library — the AGI orchestrator (U-AGI03), the speed-feed engines, and ToolChangeMinimizationEngine (U-AGI14) all depend on its tool choices. A wrong tool selection produces wrong speeds/feeds and a wrong cycle-time estimate.
csDepth: There are already multiple tool-selection engines (toolselectionadvisor, toolselectionrecommender, inventoryawaretoolselector) — dedup is mandatory (R8/duplicationGuardEngine): this unit must be a chain that COMPOSES them, not a fourth parallel selector, or it duplicates an existing engine.

ISO 13399 tool-data lookup is a constraint-matching problem against the tool library — the match must be deterministic and surface ties (two equally-good tools) rather than silently picking; the chain order is the tie-break and must be documented.

CADCAM-AGI-MS0::U-AGI13.systemImpact: RapidMovementOptimizerEngine reorders rapid moves to cut air time within CADCAM-AGI — CycleTimeOptimizerEngine (U-AGI15) consumes its optimized motion, and the program safety gate (U-AGI24) must verify every reordered rapid still clears stock and fixture. A reorder that creates a collision path is a crash hazard, so safety beats the time saving.
csDepth: Rapid-move sequencing is a TSP/nearest-neighbor route optimization — exact TSP is NP-hard, so a heuristic (nearest-neighbor + 2-opt) is correct, but the heuristic's output is meaningless if any reordered rapid clips geometry; every candidate reordering must pass a collision check before acceptance.

Collision-safe retract planning is the hard constraint — the optimizer must treat retract-clearance as inviolable and reject any reordering that violates it; an optimizer that optimizes time first and checks safety after can present an unsafe path as 'optimal'.

CADCAM-AGI-MS0::U-AGI14.systemImpact: ToolChangeMinimizationEngine reorders operations to batch same-tool work within CADCAM-AGI — CycleTimeOptimizerEngine (U-AGI15) consumes the reduced tool-change count. A reorder that violates op dependencies (finish before rough) produces a program that machines the part in the wrong order.
csDepth: Operation reordering to minimize tool changes is a constrained grouping problem — it must respect a partial order (rough-before-finish, drill-before-tap); the algorithm reorders only WITHIN dependency-compatible groups, so it is a topological-sort-then-group, not a free permutation.

Minimizing tool-change count is a set-cover-flavored problem, but the dominant correctness risk is the dependency constraint, not optimality — a slightly-suboptimal grouping is fine; a grouping that reverses rough/finish order is a defective program. Also dedup against the existing toolcalldeduplicator/batchoptimizer engines (R8).

CADCAM-AGI-MS0::U-AGI15.systemImpact: CycleTimeOptimizerEngine estimates and optimizes cycle time within CADCAM-AGI — it consumes RapidMovementOptimizerEngine (U-AGI13) and ToolChangeMinimizationEngine (U-AGI14) output, and its estimate feeds cost/quote estimation. A wrong cycle-time estimate propagates a wrong cost to the customer-facing quote.
csDepth: Cycle-time estimation is a summation of feed-time + rapid-time + dwell + tool-change overhead — accuracy requires modeling acceleration/deceleration (a short move never reaches programmed feed); a constant-velocity model systematically under-estimates time on parts with many short moves.

Estimates must be validated against measured machine cycle times — a model tuned only against itself drifts; the test should compare predicted vs real cycle time on a known program, not assert a hardcoded number.

CADCAM-AGI-MS0::U-AGI16.systemImpact: PartComplexityClassifierEngine scores part complexity within CADCAM-AGI — the AGI orchestrator (U-AGI03) and cost/scheduling estimators use the complexity score to allocate effort and estimate machining time. A mis-scored part biases cost estimates and capacity planning.
csDepth: ML complexity scoring (feature vector → score) must be monotonic in the obvious direction — adding a feature/pocket/hole must not decrease the score; the test should assert monotonicity rather than a hardcoded constant, which would pass even if the model returned a fixed value.

Feature engineering from part geometry is the load-bearing part — the feature vector (hole count, surface area, min-radius, tolerance band count) determines the model's ceiling; a regression/gradient-boosted model on weak features can't recover from a poor feature set.

CADCAM-AGI-MS0::U-AGI17.systemImpact: MasterPostProcessorEnhancement tunes per-controller G/M-code output within CADCAM-AGI — every program the AGI pipeline emits is post-processed through it for the target machine controller. Wrongly-tuned post output is G-code a real controller rejects or, worse, misinterprets, so generated G-code must parse for every target dialect.
csDepth: Controller-dialect optimization is keyed off the post-processor capability matrix — the enhancement must read the matrix per controller, not assume a generic dialect; a Fanuc-tuned output sent to an Okuma controller is the documented S[Vnn]-vs-S\d regex-trap class of bug.

Generated G-code must be parse-verified per target controller dialect — a post that emits syntactically-plausible-but-wrong code is silently dangerous; the test must run the output through each controller's parser.

CADCAM-AGI-MS0::U-AGI18.systemImpact: VariabilityIntegrationLayer adapts CADCAM-AGI to ever-changing conditions — it re-tunes parameters and strategy from outcome feedback, so the AGI orchestrator (U-AGI03) and StrategyEvolutionEngine depend on it for closed-loop improvement. If it adapts on noise or never adapts, the AGI pipeline either drifts or stagnates.
csDepth: Online adaptation must distinguish a real condition shift from outcome noise — re-tuning on every single outcome chases noise; use a drift-detection gate (conformal/CUSUM-style) so re-tuning fires only on a statistically significant shift, the same discipline as the conformal drift gate.

Feedback-driven re-tuning paired with continual learning (U-ML-11) risks catastrophic forgetting — adapting to new conditions must not erase competence on prior conditions; the layer should bound how far a re-tune can move from the prior config.

CADCAM-AGI-MS0::U-AGI19.systemImpact: SoftwareRouterEngine picks the CAD/CAM software for a job within CADCAM-AGI — the AGI orchestrator (U-AGI03) uses its choice to route work to the right bridge engine (Mastercam/FreeCAD/Inventor/SolidCAM/hyperMILL). A wrong routing decision sends a job to a bridge that can't do it.
csDepth: Capability-match routing must surface ties — when two software packages are equally capable for a feature, the router must return the conflict (R7), not silently pick; a silent pick hides a real decision the operator should make.

The feature-to-software capability lookup is a matrix that must be the single source of truth shared with the AGI bridges — if the router's capability map drifts from what a bridge actually supports, routing succeeds but the bridge fails.

CADCAM-AGI-MS0::U-AGI20.systemImpact: cadCamAgiDispatcher is the MCP execution surface for the entire CADCAM-AGI-MS0 milestone — it is how every U-AGI engine becomes externally callable. If an action is in the executor but missing from the z.enum(), the action is unreachable in production while a mock-based test passes; this dispatcher is the wiring that makes the whole milestone usable.
csDepth: Every action must be in BOTH the z.enum(ACTIONS) AND have an executor body — the documented RGS-TOOL bug is that MockMCPServer bypasses the SDK enum gate, so a missing-from-enum action 9/9-passes in tests while production is 100% broken; the round-trip E2E must drive the real enum gate.

The dispatcher action enum + Zod input schema is a contract — a schema change without an N-1 migration breaks every caller; validate input at the boundary and fail loud on a schema mismatch rather than passing a malformed payload to the executor.

CADCAM-AGI-MS0::U-AGI21.systemImpact: The CADCAM-AGI full-pipeline integration test is the end-to-end oracle for the whole milestone — it drives CAD→CAM→post through the real engines (U-AGI01..U-AGI20) and is the regression net the milestone close-out depends on. If it runs against hermetic fakes, the milestone ships with the integration unverified.
csDepth: Multi-stage E2E assertion must verify each stage's output is consumed correctly by the next — a test that only checks the final output can pass even if a middle stage no-op'd and a later stage compensated; assert intermediate contracts.

Hermetic fakes do not prove production wiring — the documented lesson (RGS-TOOL MS1: 97 hermetic tests missed 10 P0 bugs in the real reader factories) — the integration test must drive at least the real dispatcher and real engine APIs as the regression oracle.

CADCAM-AGI-MS0::U-AGI22.systemImpact: The /agi-program skill is the operator-facing entry to the CADCAM-AGI pipeline — it routes to cadCamAgiDispatcher (U-AGI20). Invalid command frontmatter means the skill fails the command-frontmatter schema and may not load/trigger correctly, leaving the whole AGI milestone without a usable invocation surface.
csDepth: The skill frontmatter must validate against .claude/schemas/command-frontmatter.schema.json — a frontmatter field error makes the skill silently mis-trigger or not load; validate it explicitly, don't assume.

Skill-to-dispatcher invocation must reference the actual cadCamAgiDispatcher action names — a skill that names a non-existent action looks fine in the .md but fails at runtime; cross-check against the U-AGI20 enum.

CADCAM-AGI-MS0::U-AGI23.systemImpact: The AGI System Guide is the documentation surface for the whole CADCAM-AGI-MS0 milestone — it is the operator/developer reference for U-AGI01..U-AGI24 and the doc surface the doc-reflection rule requires updating whenever any AGI unit changes. A stale guide misleads future work on the AGI system.
csDepth: Documentation-as-code: the guide must be a concise CLAUDE.md-pointer-style index into wiki detail pages, not a monolith — past ~200 lines, dense docs stop being read and CLAUDE.md compliance collapses.

The four-surface doc-reflection rule means CLAUDE.md + MEMORY.md + wiki + Obsidian memory must all be updated in the same session — an AGI guide that updates only the wiki leaves the pointer index stale.

CADCAM-AGI-MS0::U-AGI24.systemImpact: The AGI Safety Gate is the hard block on unsafe CADCAM-AGI output — every program the AGI orchestrator (U-AGI03) emits passes through it before reaching a machine. It is the last line of defense against the rapid-move/feed/post regressions in U-AGI13/U-AGI01/U-AGI17; if it weakens from block to warn, an unsafe program can reach the shop floor.
csDepth: A hard-gate must be block, not warn — it refuses unsafe output unconditionally and loud; the safety-tier discipline forbids softening a block to a warn, and the gate must be on the un-disableable allowlist so a profile can't turn it off.

Safety-envelope constraint checks must use canonical constants from physics/constants.ts — inlining a safety threshold creates a drift hazard where the gate checks against a different limit than the rest of the system; the envelope (max feed, max RPM, collision clearance) is safety-critical and single-sourced.

CADCAM-DAGI-MS1::U-DASAL02.systemImpact: CadQueryActionExecutorEngine synthesizes a CadQuery DSL method chain from PRISM actions — it is the execution arm of the DAGI action layer, consuming CadQueryBridgeEngine (CADCAM-AGI U-AGI04) to actually run the synthesized chain. A chain that compiles but produces wrong geometry silently corrupts the part the DAGI pipeline builds.
csDepth: DSL chain synthesis (fluent builder) is a sequence-to-code translation — the generated chain must be verified to EXECUTE and produce the intended geometry, not merely parse; a syntactically valid CadQuery chain can build the wrong solid.

AST/sequence-to-DSL translation has an ordering hazard — CadQuery operations are order-dependent (a fillet after a chamfer differs from before); the synthesizer must preserve the action sequence's intended order, and an executor crossing the Python process boundary must fail loud on a kernel error.

CADCAM-DAGI-MS1::U-DASAL09.systemImpact: HyperMillActionExecutorEngine maps PRISM DAGI actions to the hyperMILL automation API — it is the hyperMILL execution arm of the DAGI action layer, backed by the consolidated hyperMILL action-sequence knowledge (U-CTE10). A mis-mapped action silently fails to produce the intended hyperMILL operation.
csDepth: Action-to-API command mapping must be total and fail loud on an unmapped action — a hyperMILL automation interface that silently ignores an unknown action produces a program missing that operation.

hyperMILL automation is process-stateful (like Mastercam COM) — the executor must detect hyperMILL-not-running and a wedged automation session, and verify each action's real effect rather than treating a non-throwing call as success.

CADCAM-DAGI-MS1::U-DASAL11.systemImpact: InventorActionExecutorEngine drives Inventor via Apprentice (read) + iLogic (write) — it is the Inventor execution arm of the DAGI action layer. Mixing the read-only and write paths, or a write action that doesn't regenerate the model, silently corrupts the part the DAGI pipeline builds in Inventor.
csDepth: Inventor Apprentice is a read-only API and iLogic is the write path — the executor must keep the read/write split explicit; routing a write action to Apprentice silently no-ops, routing a read through iLogic risks an unintended model mutation.

Write actions must verify the model actually regenerated and didn't enter an error state (over-defined sketch, constraint conflict) — the same regeneration-verification hazard as InventorILogicBridgeEngine (U-AGI07); a 'returned' COM call is not a 'succeeded' regeneration.

CADCAM-DAGI-MS1::U-DASAL12.systemImpact: SolidCAMiMachiningBridgeEngine encodes SolidCAM iMachining adaptive-chipload/engagement knowledge — the DAGI action layer and any CAM strategy unit that picks iMachining technology depend on it. Because iMachining parameters drive real cutting, inlining chipload/engagement constants instead of importing from physics/constants.ts is a safety-relevant drift hazard.
csDepth: iMachining's technology-wizard parameters (adaptive chipload, engagement angle, step) are physics-relevant — they must import from physics/constants.ts; inlining a chipload constant duplicates a safety-rail value and the bridge can silently diverge from the canonical limit (the U-WIRE-ENERGY KC11 inline-vs-canonical bug class).

The iMachining bridge encodes a knowledge mapping (feature/material → iMachining technology) — it must surface when no iMachining technology fits rather than silently emitting a default; an inappropriate technology choice produces aggressive toolpaths.
